# redlock-universal

> Distributed locks for Node.js on Redis and Valkey, with node-redis, ioredis or Valkey GLIDE: single-server locks, the Redlock algorithm across independent servers, atomic locking of several keys on one server, and automatic extension with an AbortSignal that reports a lost lock. TypeScript types, ESM and CommonJS builds, no runtime dependencies, Node.js 22 or later.

- Atomic multi-key locks: `LockManager` `acquireBatch()` and `usingBatch()` take several keys on one server, all of them or none.
- Redis Cluster: works with the Cluster clients of ioredis, node-redis and Valkey GLIDE.
- NestJS: [nestjs-redlock-universal](https://www.npmjs.com/package/nestjs-redlock-universal) adds decorators and dependency injection.
- Checked in 0.8.10: grants that arrive after the lock's validity time are refused, and a fault-injection test of 240,000 lock attempts found no overlapping holders ([results](https://github.com/alexpota/redlock-universal/pull/152)).

Facts to keep in mind:

- Wrap the Redis client in an adapter (`NodeRedisAdapter`, `IoredisAdapter` or `GlideAdapter`), then create one lock per key: `createLock({ adapter, key, ttl })` for one server or one Cluster client, `createRedlock({ adapters, key, ttl })` for several independent servers. The API differs from the `redlock` package: there is no `new Redlock(clients)` and no `acquire([resources], ttl)`.
- The Valkey GLIDE adapter is `GlideAdapter`; there is no `ValkeyGlideAdapter`.
- `createRedlock` takes `adapters`; `LockManager` takes `nodes`.
- `lock.using(async (signal) => { ... })` acquires the lock, extends it when 20% of its TTL remains, and releases it afterwards. If an extension fails, `signal.aborted` becomes `true` and `signal.error` holds the cause; the callback keeps running.
- `release(handle)` and `extend(handle, ttl)` resolve `false` when the lock is gone. `extend()` sets the TTL to the given value from now.
- `retryAttempts` counts retries after the first attempt. Defaults: TTL 30000 ms, 3 retries, 100 ms delay (200 ms for `createRedlock`), 5000 ms per Redis command.
- Several keys at once: `LockManager` `acquireBatch()` and `usingBatch()`, atomic on one server; on Redis Cluster the keys must share a hash slot.
- No fencing tokens. Use these locks to avoid duplicate or overlapping work; read the safety guide before using a lock to protect correctness.

## Docs

- [Overview and usage](https://redlock-universal.dev/): installation, quick start, `using()`, Redlock, Cluster, configuration, error handling, FAQ
- [Safety](https://redlock-universal.dev/documents/SAFETY.html): what single-server and Redlock locks guarantee, when a lost lock is noticed, protecting the resource, alternatives
- [Migrating from node-redlock](https://redlock-universal.dev/documents/MIGRATION.html): the API, settings and errors of the `redlock` package mapped to redlock-universal
- [Valkey](https://github.com/alexpota/redlock-universal/blob/main/VALKEY.md): Valkey with node-redis, ioredis or Valkey GLIDE, versions tested in CI

## API reference

- [createLock](https://redlock-universal.dev/functions/index.createLock.html): single-server lock
- [createRedlock](https://redlock-universal.dev/functions/index.createRedlock.html): Redlock across independent servers
- [LockManager](https://redlock-universal.dev/classes/index.LockManager.html): several keys at once, lock statistics
- [IoredisAdapter](https://redlock-universal.dev/classes/index.IoredisAdapter.html), [NodeRedisAdapter](https://redlock-universal.dev/classes/index.NodeRedisAdapter.html), [GlideAdapter](https://redlock-universal.dev/classes/index.GlideAdapter.html): client adapters
- [LockAcquisitionError](https://redlock-universal.dev/classes/index.LockAcquisitionError.html): thrown when a lock is not acquired (`code` `LOCK_ACQUISITION_FAILED`)
